simple.meaning: אֲלוּ (ʼălûw) is a Hebrew word meaning “lo!.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אֲלוּ (H431) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 2:31, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲלוּ (H431) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אֲלוּ (H431) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אֲלוּ (ʼălûw) / H431 is traced through Daniel 2:31, Daniel 4:7, Daniel 4:10, Daniel 7:8 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H431. alu אֲלוּ Interjection lo! (derivation uncertain: usually regarded as by-form of אֲרוּ , q. v.; compare Egyptian Aramaic הלו , Cooke No.73 , RES 492 B = S-C M b ); — וַאֲלוּ Dan 2:31 וַאֲלוּ הֲוַיְתָ חָזֵי , 4:7 ; 4:10 ; 7:8 always in description of a vision.

occurrences.englishText: “You, O king, saw, and behold,* “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was excellent, stood before you; and its appearance was terrifying.
Then the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers came in; and I told the dream before them; but they didn’t make known to me its interpretation.
Thus were the visions of my head on my bed: I saw, and behold, a tree in the middle of the earth; and its height was great.

“I considered the horns, and behold, there came up among them another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots: and behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.
